diagnosis_explanation: You recently had surgery on your right knee. This surgery is called a total knee replacement. It is also called a total knee arthroplasty. Your knee was replaced because it was causing you pain.
medication_rationale:
Coumadin 4 mg a day:
This medicine is prescribed to prevent blood clots. It is important for your recovery after knee surgery. You may notice your skin turning a bit orange or yellow. This is a normal effect of the medicine. Call your doctor right away if you have severe pain, swelling, or a cut that will not stop bleeding.

Vicodin 5/500 mg q.4-6h:
This medicine is for pain after your knee surgery. It will help you feel more comfortable. You may feel sleepy or dizzy. This is common when you first take it. Call your doctor if you have trouble breathing or feel very confused.
recovery_trajectory:
**Week 1:**
- You will likely feel tired and have some pain. This is normal.
- You can put weight on your right leg as you are able.
- Use crutches or a walker to help you move around.
- Do not lift anything heavier than 5 pounds.
- Call your doctor if you see more redness or swelling.
- Call your doctor if you have drainage from your incision.
- Call your doctor if you get a fever.
- Your goal is to walk a little more each day inside your home.

**Week 2:**
- Your pain should start to get a bit better.
- You can likely walk a bit further with less help.
- Continue to put weight on your right leg as tolerated.
- Call your doctor if you have any concerns about your knee.
- Your goal is to walk for 10 minutes three times a day.
- Avoid activities that strain your knee.

**Week 3:**
- You may feel more energy and less pain this week.
- You can likely do more light activities around the house.
- Continue to put weight on your right leg as tolerated.
- Your goal is to walk for 15 minutes without stopping.
- Call your doctor if redness or swelling gets worse.
- Call your doctor if you have new drainage from your incision.

**Week 4:**
- Most days should feel easier than the week before.
- You can likely walk longer distances with less pain.
- Continue to put weight on your right leg as tolerated.
- Your goal is to walk outside for short periods.
- Call your doctor if you get a fever or feel unwell.
- Call your doctor if you have any worries about your knee.

**When to expect improvement:**
- You should feel a steady improvement over the next few weeks.
- Keep moving your knee gently to maintain flexibility.
- Follow your doctor's instructions for physical therapy.
- Progress will be gradual.
escalation_guide:
CALL 911 IMMEDIATELY
These symptoms are life-threatening. Do not drive yourself.
- Increased redness with fever: You may have a bad infection.
- Drainage from incision site: This is a sign of infection.
- Wound looks infected: Red streaks mean bad infection spreading.
- Pain around the incision: Your joint may be infected badly.

GO TO THE ER TODAY
Do not wait until tomorrow. Go within a few hours.
- Increased redness without fever: The area may be infected.
- Swelling around the incision: Fluid may be building up there.
- Concerns about operation: Your knee may need urgent care.
- Concerns about incision site: The wound may be opening up.

CALL YOUR DOCTOR
Call during office hours. Do not go to the ER for these.
- Mild redness on knee: This can happen while you heal.
- Mild swelling of knee: This can happen while you heal.
- Drainage that is clear: This is not a bad sign.
